title: Influence of occlusion changes on upper body posture parameters in standing and walking in healthy young subjects measured using video raster stereography. A pre-post study with a 3-month follow-up
summary: Untersuchung von verschiedenen experimentell eingestellten Bisspositionen (okklusale Positionen), wie z.B. eine minimale Bisserhöhung bis hin zu einer Aufbissschiene unmittelbar (kurzfristig) und/oder langfristig und deren messbare Veränderungen der Stand- und Gangparameter bei gesunden Erwachsenen

interventions.name:
1. Analysis of gait parameters as a function of different occlusal positions, such as the occlusal position at rest, various interferences, and a bite splint (e.g., step time/step length, variability of gait cycles)
2. Investigation of planar pressure and load distribution during walking depending

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- subjects between the ages of 18 and 40
- Angle Class II (distal bite position)
- No restrictions of the musculoskeletal system or upper respiratory tract on the day of the examination
- Signed declaration of consent
Exclusion criteria:
- subjects under the age of 18
- subjects with syndromic diseases and cleft lip, jaw, or palate
- subjects with jaw joint replacement
- Insufficient knowledge of the German language
- Lack of capacity to give consent
- Acute complaints or diseases of the musculoskeletal system or craniomandibular system
- Injuries/surgeries of the musculoskeletal system or craniomandibular system within the last two years
- Ongoing orthodontic, orthopedic, or physiotherapeutic treatment
-    Use of muscle relaxants or other medications that affect muscle tone or movement patterns
-    Acute or chronic infections of the upper respiratory tract (e.g., polyps or chronic sinusitis)
-    Structural abnormalities in the nose or throat (e.g., deviated septum)
-    Sleep-related breathing disorders
